title: Theories and axiomatization: deciding sentences and describing classes

based_on.title: Lecture Notes: An Introduction to Model Theory

summary: Distinguish axioms from their consequences, characterize complete theories by agreement of their models, and test finite axiomatizability using complements.
abstract: One sentence can require exactly two objects, while an infinite list of size requirements describes infinite domains. Could a different, finite list describe those same infinite structures? Compactness shows why this is impossible and gives a general test: a class and its complement can both be described by first-order axioms exactly when a finite list suffices. A separate question is whether the axioms settle every sentence in their language. For axioms that have a model, this happens precisely when all their models agree on sentences, although those models can still have different sizes. Keeping an axiom list separate from all its consequences makes these two questions easier to distinguish.
